title: An Ahom Cosmogony with translation and vocabulary
author: Sir George Abraham Grierson
description: Critical edition and interlinear linguistic analysis of the ancient Tai cosmological text Phura Tara Along published in the Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society. Documents archaic lexicon of primordial waters, deities, and world emergence with lexical parallels in Khamyang and Shan.

sentences.text_roman: tsaw tii phaa phaw mroeng nam khyaa

sentences.free_translation_en: In the ancient beginning, the celestial voice spoke over the primeval watery void.
sentences.free_translation_as: প্ৰাচীন আৰম্ভণিত আদিম জলধিৰ ওপৰত স্বৰ্গীয় বাণী প্ৰতিধ্বনিত হৈছিল।
sentences.speaker: Sir George A. Grierson (Orientalist)
sentences.notes: Opening verse of the Phura-tara-along creation narrative.

sentences.speaker: Sir George A. Grierson
sentences.notes: Cosmogonic imagery of the primordial waters before land formation.

sentences.speaker: Sir George A. Grierson
sentences.notes: Phaa-chau equated with supreme creator spirit Pha-Teng-Kham.

sentences.free_translation_en: Out from the water, mountains arose and took their place in the center.

sentences.speaker: Sir George A. Grierson
sentences.notes: Myth of cosmic mountain Meru (Khao Phra Sumen).

sentences.speaker: Sir George A. Grierson
sentences.notes: Descent of divine ancestors Khun Lung and Khun Lai.

sentences.notes: Gift of sacred rice seeds bestowed by heaven.

sentences.speaker: Sir George A. Grierson
sentences.notes: Spiritual devotion reflected in archaic Tai liturgy.
